name: Lateral canthoplasty
lead: Lateral canthoplasty is eyelid surgery that repositions, tightens or re-anchors the lateral canthus, the outer corner of the eye where the upper and lower lids meet. In ophthalmic and plastic surgery it is used to support or tighten a lax lower eyelid, to prevent or correct lid malposition after lower blepharoplasty, and in facial palsy and ectropion repair.[1][3][6][10]

In looksmaxxing communities the procedure is discussed as a route to a more positive canthal tilt, in which the outer corner of the eye sits higher than the inner corner, and to a more almond or 'hunter' eye shape with firmer lower-lid support and, sometimes, more visible sclera. Members compare canthoplasty with the more conservative canthopexy, trade before-and-after photos, and debate suitability by age.[12][14][15][29]

Surgeons distinguish canthoplasty, which involves releasing and reattaching the lateral canthal tendon, from canthopexy, which supports the lid with sutures without detaching the tendon. Reviews note that small adjustments here can produce large changes in lower-lid shape, and that excessive tightening or midface elevation can lead to round-eye deformity or ectropion.[1][2] The published surgical literature, which runs from technique papers in the 1990s to reviews in 2021, centres on lid support and function; no study located evaluates canthoplasty specifically for increasing canthal tilt in people with normal eyelid tone.[1][6][23][26]

paras: The canthus is the corner of the eye; the outer one is the lateral canthus and the inner one the medial canthus. The lateral commissure is more acute than the medial one, and the lids lie in close contact with the globe there.[10] Reviewers describe understanding the anatomy and function of the lateral canthal tendon as critical to choosing a technique.[6]

Wikipedia defines canthoplasty as plastic surgery on the medial canthus, the lateral canthus or both, used for cosmetic purposes as well as for eyelid function or malposition, and separates it from canthotomy, in which the canthus is cut to relieve orbital pressure from conditions such as orbital haemorrhage.[10]

A review of aesthetic canthal suspension describes the options as canthopexy, an orbicularis sling and modified canthoplasty. Canthopexy is the most conservative and supports the lower eyelid over the short or long term; the orbicularis sling avoids surgery around the complex lateral canthus but may not suit every case; canthoplasty is generally reserved for more marked laxity, which is less common in people seeking cosmetic blepharoplasty.[1] A second review covers open and closed canthal suspension, commissure-sparing open canthoplasty and canthopexy, together with preoperative evaluation, postoperative course and complications.[6]

A 1999 paper in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery presented an algorithm for choosing between canthoplasty and canthopexy in lower eyelid and midfacial rejuvenation and described a simplified suture canthopexy called the lateral retinacular suspension.[21] Earlier technique papers from 1997 described the inferior retinacular lateral canthoplasty and reviewed the evolution of lateral canthoplasty techniques and indications.[22][23]

Lateral canthal procedures were first developed mainly for functional problems such as lid laxity and paralytic eyelid malposition. Papers indexed in the 1990s describe lateral canthoplasty as a standalone procedure,[24] and a 1999 prospective trial combined upper-lid gold weight implantation with lower-lid lateral canthoplasty for patients with facial palsy.[7]

As transcutaneous lower blepharoplasty became widespread, surgeons reported a higher risk of lower lid malposition and began to advocate routine lateral canthal support. A 10-year review of one surgeon's primary lower blepharoplasty practice with routine lateral canthal support is among the larger reports of this approach.[4] A 1998 paper on redraping the inferior orbicularis arc recommended pairing the muscle redraping with lateral canthoplasty,[25] and a 2003 paper on lateral canthal anchoring addressed fixation of the canthus.[26] The 2003 midfacial rejuvenation review stressed that any midface advancement should allow a canthoplasty or canthopexy to heal without downward traction.[2]

More recent reviews, published in 2015 and 2021, frame canthal suspension as an adjunct to lower blepharoplasty and place stress on understanding the anatomy and ageing changes of the lateral canthal tendon before choosing a technique.[1][6]

Canthal procedures are used for involutional lower lid laxity and ectropion, and a randomised trial has examined lateral tarsal strip surgery, a related tightening procedure, for epiphora (watery eye) in involutional ectropion.[8] In a prospective trial of 40 patients (ages 19 to 72) with paralytic lagophthalmos, upper-lid gold weights were implanted in all patients and lower lid lateral canthoplasty was performed in 14 who also had lid laxity.[7] Further reviews address management of lower eyelid laxity and the treatment of lower eyelid retraction after blepharoplasty, in which the authors describe lateral canthoplasty as a point of failure under tension.[5][27]

In aesthetic surgery, canthal support is advocated as a routine part of lower blepharoplasty to reduce the risk of lid malposition.[4][21] Reviews also describe canthal support for people with prominent globes or a negative vector, in which the cheek sits behind the eye, and in lower eyelids with increased laxity.[1] Surgeons caution that only a limited amount of midface lift is safe before round-eye deformity and ectropion result.[2] Wikipedia notes that canthoplasty is common in cosmetic procedures as well as functional ones.[10]

subs.h: As discussed for canthal tilt and eye shape
paras: The communities' interest lies in a different outcome from the one reported in surgical series: lifting the outer corner relative to the inner corner, reducing a 'droopy' or negatively tilted look, and showing more sclera under the iris. Forum posters describe their goal as making the lower lid sit higher so the eye looks the way it does when the lid is pushed up with a finger.[12] Others ask about eyes that measure positive on paper but 'look negative' because of hooding and low brows.[14] These aims are stated by patients and forum members; the surgical papers describe support, tightening and repair rather than measured changes in tilt.[1][6]

Reviews state that evaluation before canthal suspension covers lid laxity, globe prominence, the vector between lower lid and cheek, and the position of the lateral canthus.[1][6] The 2021 review also covers the postoperative course and complications, including complications.[6] A 10-year retrospective series of 892 blepharoplasty cases reported on dry-eye symptoms and chemosis after surgery, a problem that is relevant to any lower-lid procedure.[28]

Reviews of canthal suspension discuss complications including lid malposition, asymmetry and altered eyelid shape, because the area is delicate and small changes have large effects.[1][6] Excess elevation or tightening is associated with round-eye deformity, vertical shortening of the lower lid and ectropion.[2] Post-blepharoplasty lower eyelid retraction is described as difficult to treat, and one set of authors reconstruct the eyelid with an implant and a hard palate graft to avoid tension on the lateral canthoplasty.[5]

Forum threads with titles such as 'botch rate' reflect community concern about outcomes, and one reply to a poster asking about droopy eyes says it would try everything else before canthoplasty because the procedure is risky.[13][14]

The published human literature on lateral canthoplasty concerns eyelid function and lower blepharoplasty support, including reviews, surgeon case series and small trials.[1][3][4][7][8] Examples include the 10-year review of routine canthal support during lower blepharoplasty,[4] the prospective facial palsy trial of 40 patients,[7] and the randomised trial of lateral tarsal strip surgery for epiphora in involutional ectropion.[8] No study located examines lateral canthoplasty as a cosmetic procedure to change canthal tilt in people with normal eyelid tone.

On looksmax.org, members ask whether canthoplasty or canthopexy is better for improving sclera show or canthal tilt, and debate whether canthoplasty is appropriate for people under 40.[12][15] One reply to a poster asking about sclera show recommends canthopexy combined with fat grafts.[12] Threads discuss before-and-after photos, whether to proceed at all[32], and planning canthoplasty alongside other facial surgeries such as genioplasty.[29][30][31]

Do-it-yourself canthoplasty has also become a topic on the forum, with at least one thread asking why the trend arose.[16] The wiki does not describe self-performed surgery; no research or surgical guideline recommends it, and the literature describes canthal surgery as delicate work by trained surgeons.[1][6]

Related procedures include lower blepharoplasty, midface lifting, orbicularis redraping and the lateral tarsal strip, all of which appear in the surgical literature alongside canthal support.[1][2][4][8][25] Medial canthoplasty exists but is described by forum members as uncommon, with most work targeting the lateral canthus.[12]

timeline.event: A paper titled 'Lateral canthoplasty' appears in the Journal of Dermatologic Surgery and Oncology.[24]
Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery publishes papers on the inferior retinacular lateral canthoplasty and on the evolution of lateral canthoplasty techniques and indications.[22][23]
Redraping of the inferior orbicularis arc is described, to be accompanied by lateral canthoplasty.[25]
An algorithm for choosing canthal support and the lateral retinacular suspension canthopexy are presented;[21] a prospective facial palsy trial combines gold weights and lateral canthoplasty.[7]
Reviews on lateral canthoplasty and midfacial rejuvenation appear, the latter warning of round-eye deformity with excess midface lift.[2][3]
A 10-year review of primary lower blepharoplasty with routine lateral canthal support is published.[4]
Clinics in Plastic Surgery publishes a review of aesthetic canthal suspension.[1]
A randomised trial compares lateral tarsal strip with and without punctoplasty for epiphora in involutional ectropion.[8]
Facial Plastic Surgery Clinics of North America publishes reviews on the spectrum of aesthetic canthal suspension and on post-blepharoplasty lower eyelid retraction.[5][6]
Looksmax.org threads ask why DIY canthoplasty became a trend.[16]

lore.intro: The procedure is discussed on looksmax.org mainly as a way to alter canthal tilt and sclera show, with recurring disagreement over canthoplasty versus canthopexy, over age suitability and over risk.[12][14][15]

claims.claim: Canthoplasty can raise the outer eye corner for a more positive canthal tilt.
claims.believers: Members ask which procedure would change tilt or sclera show and some say canthopexy with fat grafts is preferable.[12]
claims.experts: Surgical reviews describe canthal procedures as supporting or tightening the lower lid; no study found tests canthoplasty for increasing canthal tilt cosmetically.[1][6]

claims.claim: Canthopexy is the better choice than canthoplasty for people under 40.
claims.believers: A thread title argues that those under 40 should choose canthopexy and some members repeat that canthoplasty is for people 30 and older.[15][11]
claims.experts: Reviews state canthopexy is the most conservative option and canthoplasty is reserved for marked laxity, which is less common in younger aesthetic patients.[1]

claims.claim: Canthoplasty carries a meaningful risk of botching the eye.
claims.believers: Members start threads on botch rate and one replier calls it risky and advises trying other options first.[13][14]
claims.experts: Reviews note that small adjustments around the canthus can alter lower eyelid shape substantially and that malposition is a known risk.[1][2]

claims.claim: Canthoplasty can be done at home.
claims.believers: Multiple threads about 'DIY canthoplasty' exist, with one asking why it became a trend.[16]
claims.experts: No published studies or surgical guidelines describe or support self-performed canthal surgery; the literature describes it as delicate surgery performed by trained surgeons.[1][6]

claims.claim: Raising the outer corner makes eyes look more 'hunter' and attractive.
claims.believers: Members post before-and-after threads and ask for evaluations, treating a higher lateral canthus as a facial goal.[29][30]
claims.experts: Published surgical papers measure lid position, support and complications; no study located measures attractiveness or tilt change after cosmetic canthoplasty.[1][6]

claims.claim: Canthopexy with fat grafts can improve sclera show.
claims.believers: A reply in a looksmax.org thread recommends canthopexy with fat grafts for a poster who wants the look of a pushed-up lower lid.[12]
claims.experts: Reviews describe canthopexy as the conservative support option and describe fat and volume procedures in other settings; none evaluates this combination for sclera show.[1][5]

claims.claim: Canthoplasty can be combined with other facial surgeries in one plan.
claims.believers: A thread poster describes planning genioplasty, canthoplasty and another procedure together and asks for opinions.[31]
claims.experts: Surgical papers describe canthal support combined with lower blepharoplasty, orbicularis redraping or midface lifting.[4][25][2]

card.summary: Surgery on the outer eye corner, used medically for lid laxity and increasingly sought to raise canthal tilt; no studies test it for that cosmetic aim.
card.note: Cosmetic tilt change is untested; lid malposition risk is documented and DIY versions circulate online.

quick.overview:
Lateral canthoplasty reshapes or tightens the outer corner of the eye by working on the lateral canthal tendon. Surgeons use it to support a loose lower eyelid, for ectropion, and alongside lower blepharoplasty.

In looksmaxxing forums people ask about it for a more positive canthal tilt or a more almond eye. The published literature covers lid support, not cosmetic tilt, and forum users debate canthoplasty versus the gentler canthopexy.
quick.mechanism: The lateral canthal tendon is repositioned or tightened and anchored to the orbital rim, lifting and supporting the outer lid. Canthopexy uses sutures without detaching the tendon.
quick.risks: Reviews note that small changes can substantially alter lower eyelid shape and that malposition, round-eye deformity and ectropion are risks. Cosmetic canthal-tilt outcomes have not been studied, and self-performed versions discussed online have no published support.
